newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ENVIRONMENT FUND SPENDING MAY RISE IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ENVIRONMENT FUND SPENDING MAY RISE IN 1997.

text.p: Poland's National Environment Protection Fund estimates its spending on environment protection may increase by 500 million zlotys to 1.65 billion in 1997, the president of the fund said on Thursday.
Jozef Zegar said, however, the increase depened on whether the fund manages to obtain loans from commercial banks.
"We should be able to get additional 500 million zlotys from commercial banks, which would mean a 30-percent growth in real terms," he told a news conference.

He expected the loans, to be taken by companies doing environmental projects, would have preferential interest and the fund would cover the diffrence between market credit rates and the preferential rate.
The credit could also be extended for longer-term periods than those available on the market. Zegar said many banks were interested in the preferential loan project.

He said that of the one-billion zloty core of the fund's spending about 717 million zlotys would be used for loans, about 237 million for subsidies and about 55 million zlotys to cover preferential credit interest differences.
He said the fund planned to earmark about 389 million zlotys for water protection, 362 million for air protection, and 90 million zlotys for soil protection this year.
The remaining funds would go for monitoring, education and other projects.

The fund's expenditure for environment protection, which comes mainly from local governments payments, fines and returned loans, amounted to about 20 percent of overall Poland's environment expenditure in 1996.
